task: Add AI refine and revert endpoints for workflows, with audit logging for AI modifications and reverts (EPMCDME-12616, backend only).

key_reasoning.reason: Five distinct layers are touched: API (workflow router), Service (workflow_service), AI-Chain (new WorkflowGeneratorService or extended AssistantGeneratorService), DB-Persistence (YamlConfigHistory Pydantic model with new optional change_type field stored in JSONB), and External (LLM invocation via LiteLLM/PromptGeneratorChain). Cross-cutting observability changes also land in WorkflowMonitoringService.

Four to five components must be created or modified: workflow router (new endpoints), workflow service (new revert and refine methods), a new AI generator service with a new workflow YAML prompt template, the YamlConfigHistory model, and the monitoring service plus metrics constants. The revert path builds on existing infrastructure; the AI refine path requires a new abstraction.

No WorkflowGeneratorService or workflow-specific prompt template exists — a new pattern must be authored. Workflow YAML is significantly more complex than assistant fields, making structured-output prompt design non-trivial with mandatory LLM output validation. The revert path risks double-writing history if not carefully ordered relative to the existing _update_workflow_history prepend. Guardrail re-sync behaviour on revert is an open design question. The yaml_config_history code path has zero existing tests, so correctness must be established from scratch.

Estimated 7–10 files: workflow.py router (modify), workflow_service.py (modify), new WorkflowGeneratorService file (new), new workflow YAML prompt template (new), workflow_config.py YamlConfigHistory model (modify), workflow_monitoring_service.py (modify), metrics_constants.py (modify), plus 2–3 new test files across tests/codemie/rest_api/routers/ and tests/codemie/service/. Changes span 4+ directories.
